content: Ceftobiprole medocaril sodium is administered intravenously at a dose of 3 mg/kg every 8 hours, with a maximum dose of 667 mg per administration. The treatment duration typically ranges from 7 to 14 days. Ceftobiprole, an inhibitor of OATP1B1/1B3 transporters, can increase plasma concentrations of drugs that are substrates of these transporters. This interaction may lead to elevated drug levels and enhanced effects or toxicity of the co-administered medications. Specific interactions include: 1. Elagolix: Ceftobiprole increases the levels or effects of elagolix. Co-administration is contraindicated. 2. Ambrisentan: Ceftobiprole increases the levels or effects of ambrisentan. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 3. Atorvastatin: Ceftobiprole increases the levels or effects of atorvastatin. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 4. Bosentan: Ceftobiprole increases the levels or effects of bosentan. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 5. Caspofungin: Ceftobiprole increases the levels or effects of caspofungin. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 6. Digoxin: Ceftobiprole increases the levels or effects of digoxin. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 7. Elbasvir/Grazoprevir: Ceftobiprole increases the levels or effects of elbasvir/grazoprevir. Co-administration is contraindicated. 8. Ezetimibe: Ceftobiprole increases the levels or effects of ezetimibe. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 9. Fexofenadine: Ceftobiprole increases the levels or effects of fexofenadine. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 10. Fluvastatin: Ceftobiprole increases the levels or effects of fluvastatin. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 11. Glecaprevir/Pibrentasvir: Ceftobiprole increases the levels or effects of glecaprevir/pibrentasvir. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 12. Glyburide: Ceftobiprole increases the levels or effects of glyburide. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 13. Irinotecan: Ceftobiprole increases the levels or effects of irinotecan. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 14. Letermovir: Ceftobiprole increases the levels or effects of letermovir. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 15. Lovastatin: Ceftobiprole increases the levels or effects of lovastatin. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 16. Methotrexate: Ceftobiprole increases the levels or effects of methotrexate. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 17. Momelotinib: Ceftobiprole increases the levels or effects of momelotinib. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 18. Olmesartan: Ceftobiprole increases the levels or effects of olmesartan. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 19. Paclitaxel: Ceftobiprole increases the levels or effects of paclitaxel. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 20. Pitavastatin: Ceftobiprole increases the levels or effects of pitavastatin. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 21. Pravastatin: Ceftobiprole increases the levels or effects of pravastatin. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 22. Repaglinide: Ceftobiprole increases the levels or effects of repaglinide. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 23. Resmetirom: Ceftobiprole increases the levels or effects of resmetirom. Avoid co-administration with OATP1B1/1B3 inhibitors. 24. Revefenacin: Ceftobiprole increases the levels or effects of revefenacin. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 25. Rifampin: Ceftobiprole increases the levels or effects of rifampin. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 26. Rosuvastatin: Ceftobiprole increases the levels or effects of rosuvastatin. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 27. Simvastatin: Ceftobiprole increases the levels or effects of simvastatin. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 28. Sulbactam/Durlobactam: Ceftobiprole increases the levels or effects of sulbactam/durlobactam. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 29. Voxilaprevir: Ceftobiprole increases the levels or effects of voxilaprevir. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 30. Zavegepant (intranasal): Ceftobiprole increases the levels or effects of zavegepant. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Ceftobiprole also increases the nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity of aminoglycosides such as amikacin, gentamicin, kanamycin, neomycin, plazomicin, and streptomycin. Use caution and monitor closely when co-administering these agents. Additionally, ceftobiprole may reduce the therapeutic effects of immune checkpoint inhibitors, including atezolizumab, avelumab, balstilimab, camrelizumab, cemiplimab, cosibelimab, dostarlimab, durvalumab, nivolumab, pembrolizumab, penpulimab, retifanlimab, sintilimab, and tislelizumab. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended during co-administration.
